name: DHEA-S
description: DHEA-S (Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulfate) measures adrenal androgen production and evaluates adrenal function, androgen excess, and adrenal tumors. This test assesses adrenal reserve and androgen metabolism.

testdetails.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Beckman Coulter

literatureReview: DHEA-S (Dehydroepiandrosterone Sulfate) is the sulfated form of DHEA, the primary adrenal androgen. It has a longer half-life than DHEA and is more stable in circulation. Normal ranges vary by age and sex: adult males 35-430 µg/dL, adult females 18-390 µg/dL. Levels peak in young adulthood and decline with age. Elevated levels suggest congenital adrenal hyperplasia, adrenal tumors, or polycystic ovary syndrome. Low levels indicate adrenal insufficiency or hypopituitarism. Chemiluminescent immunoassay provides excellent sensitivity. DHEA-S is used in evaluation of hirsutism, virilization, infertility, and adrenal disorders. Unlike cortisol, DHEA-S production is ACTH-dependent but not subject to negative feedback regulation.
